---
title: "Writing with Markdown"
---

Most of what you produce in this course is text: notes, reports, READMEs,
answers to exercises, documentation for the programs you write. Markdown is the
simplest way to write that text well.

Markdown is a plain-text format. You write in a way that already looks readable
in the source, and a tool converts it into HTML, PDF, slides or a book. Because
it is plain text, it works with every editor, diffs cleanly, and survives in
version control.

Here is the whole idea in one example:

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
```markdown
The **craft** of computing is learned by
*making things*, not by reading about them.
```
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
The **craft** of computing is learned by
*making things*, not by reading about them.
:::
:::

The left column is what you type. The right column is what the reader sees.

## Where you will meet it

Markdown is not one tool's private format. You will run into it in:

- README files on GitHub and GitLab
- Jupyter notebooks, in every text cell
- Quarto documents like this website
- Issue trackers, wikis, chat applications and forums

The dialects differ a little at the edges, but everything in this section works
almost everywhere.
